title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G is a stable graph (the dual graph of a stable marked curve). Its parts are A, the edges (nodes); I, the tails (marked points); \vec A, the oriented edges (half-edges); and \hat A = A ⊔ I. M_G is the boundary stratum of \bar M_{g,I} of curves of type G. \hat M_G is its finite étale cover where the branches at each node are labelled; this is the normalisation-type stratum.

Bundles over M_G:
- P_G is the G_m^A-torsor of the normal (smoothing) parameters. At a node a, the normal line is T_{p_a^+} ⊗ T_{p_a^-}.
- SP_G is P_G enlarged by the G_m^I-torsor of nonzero tangent vectors at the marked points.
- P_{G,C} are the partial products over a subset C ⊂ \hat A.
- Their fundamental groupoids T_G, ST_G, T_{G,C} are central extensions of RT_G = Π_1(M_G) by Z^A, Z^{\hat A}, Z^C. Here Z is the loop in G_m, i.e. the Dehn twist.

First point of the page. Let G^b be G cut at every edge: the disjoint union of the vertices, with half-edges turned into legs. Then M_{G^b} = \hat M_G = ∏_v M_{g_v, n_v}. On it the tangent lines at the half-edges give a finer torsor SP_{G^b} with group G_m^{\vec A} (×G_m^I). SP_G is obtained from it by pushing out along the multiplication map G_m^{\vec A} → G_m^A, (t_+, t_-) ↦ t_+ t_-. This is because the normal line at a node is the tensor product of the two branch tangent lines.

Taking fundamental groupoids, ST_G is the pushout of ST_{G^b} (group Z^{\vec A}) along the sum map Z^{\vec A} → Z^A. In mapping-class language: the two boundary twists of the cut surface both map to the Dehn twist about the curve. Hence the stabiliser of a multicurve is the quotient of the mapping class group of the cut surface (with boundary) by the differences T_{a+}T_{a-}^{-1}, up to the Aut(G)/side-swap finite part, which is the difference between \hat M_G and M_G.

NB on the page: an extension by Z^A is the fibre product over RT_G of the extensions by Z, one for each edge a. So it suffices to know the extensions T_{G,\bar a} = T_{G^b,\bar a} for oriented edges \bar a. Margin: T_{∐ G_α} ≅ ∏ T_{G_α}, which is the Künneth formula for Π_1 of products.

Conclusion: everything reduces to the building blocks ST_{g,I} (≈ T_{g,ν}^!, the Teichmüller groupoids with tangential base points). These are extensions of T_{g,I} by Z^I, equivalently the fibre product of the rank-one extensions S_iT_{g,I}, i ∈ I.

The same reduction should apply to the comparison 'tores' S'T_G → ST_G, via the generalisation (edge-contraction) maps G → G' = G/C → G^♮. Here G^♮ is the one-vertex graph, i.e. the smooth type (g,I). The next page develops this as Cartesian diagrams of torsors and groupoids.
errors: No real error. One minor gap: the deduction of SP_G (and so ST_G) from SP_{G^b} holds over \hat M_G. Passing to M_G and RT_G needs equivariance under Aut(G) and the swapping of sides of each edge; the page notes 'sur \hat M_G' but does not spell out the descent.
The arrow written \mathbb{Z}^{\vec A} → \mathbb{Z}^A leaves the Z^I factor implicit. In full it is Z^{\vec A} × Z^I → Z^A × Z^I.

ideas.what: The normal line to a boundary stratum at a node is the tensor product of the two branch tangent lines. So the torsor of smoothing parameters is pushed out from the torsor of half-edge tangent vectors along G_m^{\vec A} → G_m^A.
ideas.modern_name: Normal bundle of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n} (psi-class relation -ψ_+ - ψ_-)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; standard in boundary-stratum calculus

ideas.what: The groupoid version: the multicurve stabiliser equals the mapping class group of the cut surface with boundary (an extension by Z^{half-edges}) pushed out along Z^{\vec A} → Z^A.
ideas.modern_name: Cutting homomorphism / kernel generated by T_{a+}T_{a-}^{-1}; structure of multicurve stabilisers

ideas.what: Reduction of all boundary-stratum Teichmüller groupoids to the building blocks ST_{g,I}: extensions by Z^I, i.e. groupoids with tangential base points.
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower with tangential base points; building-block principle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3, in general form

ideas.what: Product formula for disconnected graphs: T_{∐ G_α} ≅ ∏ T_{G_α}.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of standard facts: normal bundles of boundary strata, and Dehn-twist extensions of multicurve stabilisers. It is used to reduce the Teichmüller tower to its tangentially based building blocks. The program is already in the Esquisse and in later work by Nakamura and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Il est déduisibles' should read 'Ils sont déductibles/déduisibles'. The plural 'Ils' was struck and rewritten, but the sense is 'Ils sont déduisibles d'un fibré encore plus fin'.
The homomorphism is G_m^{\bar A}/G_m^{\vec A} → G_m^A (oriented edges to edges), not 'G → \hat A → C^A' as in the previous-page transcription.
'voir SP^∧_{G^b}' is plausibly 'ou SP^∧_{G^b}' (a notational alternative); uncertain.
'S(T_{g,I}),i' is more likely '{}_i S T_{g,I}' or 'S_i T_{g,I}', meaning the rank-one extension at the i-th marked point.
Margin note: 'T_{\coprod_\alpha G_\alpha} \simeq \prod_\alpha T_{G_\alpha}', preceded by 'NB' and with an arrow pointing to 'En définitive'.
G^♮ in the last lines (likely 'G^\natural', the totally contracted one-vertex graph) is consistent with the next page.
